summary: Ship. No S1 or S2. The converter is correct on everything I recomputed (15 page outputs against independent code and known oracles, plus 43,200 day numbers and 14,400 weekdays and month lengths against Meeus and Date.UTC with no mismatch), the 33-case self-test passes in about 80 ms and its mutation guard really fails 4 of 4 checks, all 24 SPEC vectors are present with unchanged expected values and every case runs the page's own functions, three replayed input sequences match a fresh load, and the first frame is a result with the torn October 1582 grid. Layout scan found no overlap, clipping or horizontal scroll at 11 viewports from 320 to 1920 wide in five states; focus is visible, keyboard paths work, hostile and odd hashes degrade to the sample or a clamped date with no console output. Remaining items are polish: on a phone the result headline sits at the very bottom of the first screen, the More panel pops back open after a visitor closes it, and a few S4 nits.

scores.note: Date plus place gives both calendars, weekday, dropped-date detection with both readings, two-year readings for 25 March places, a custom switch day, days-between, steps with the real sums, month grid; minute ten still teaches (Denmark-Norway 29 Feb 1700, Scotland 1599 vs 1600).

15 page outputs recomputed independently (JDN 2299160/2299161, 1752 skip, Julian 29 Feb 1700 = Thu 11 Mar 1700, 29 Feb 1900 = Tue 13 Mar 1900, Washington 22 Feb 1732, Newton 4 Jan 1643, Defenestration 23 May 1618 O.S. = 2 Jun, 7 Nov 1917) plus 43,200 range values with zero mismatch; empty, huge, negative, unicode, pasted-date and bad-hash inputs all handled; 40 rapid ArrowUp and 30 rapid toggles threw nothing.
Tear-off calendar leaf with sepia/teal/red inks and a drawn zig-zag gap is distinctive and reads in light and dark; hierarchy is clear; the error state leaves a big empty card at 1100px and up.

Debounced typing, Enter and blur flush, ArrowUp/Down with Shift, tap a grid day, famous dates from the explainer scroll to the app, toast on copy, Escape returns focus to More; More reopening after a manual close (d02) is the one rough edge.

No overflow or overlap from 320 to 1920 wide, 44px controls, labelled fields, abbr weekday titles, table aria-label, live region, reduced motion honoured; gaps: no aria-invalid on the bad field, two links under 44px, grid days pointer-only (documented, Day field is the keyboard path).

Warm plain copy; intro (61 words) is accurate and glosses both calendars; unverified rows say 'as of 2026-10-13, per search results'; limits section names excluded places; explainer claims check out against the engine.
152 KB total, first render under 100 ms, self-test 79 ms including a 1500-2099 round trip, no network, no storage, CSP intact, zero console output in my runs.

Desktop first frame is title, intro, 8 controls and a red card with the torn calendar; hash holds the state and reloads exactly; on a phone the headline is at the very bottom edge of the screen (d01) and the picture is below the fold.

highlights: The first frame is the product: 13 October 1582 in Rome already answered, with weekdays running straight through a drawn torn gap and the ten dropped days as struck-through chips, the 13 filled red.
The steps panel prints the real sum (a, y, m and every term) and the page's own result matches independent Meeus and Date.UTC arithmetic across 1500-2099 in both calendars.

The self-test is honest: all 24 SPEC rows kept with unchanged expected values, labelled by source, an independent Date.UTC reference, and a mutation guard (every-fourth-year leap rule) that fails 4 of 4 targeted checks.

The year-start handling is rare and right: England 11 February 1731 shows 'as written' 1731/32 and 'counted from 1 January' side by side with the correct weekdays, and Scotland 1599 vs 1600 switches the rule correctly.
Errors are specific (April 1582 has only 30 days; February 1900 leap-year note) and the pasted-date message tells people to use three boxes.
State lives in a strictly parsed hash: a bookmark restores it, bad or hostile hashes fall back to the sample, and nothing is stored or sent.

defects.title: Phone first screen pushes result to bottom edge
defects.detail: On 390px wide the intro and the form fill the screen; the result card starts at y=680 and its headline top is at y=790 of 844. On a real phone browser with toolbars (about 390x700) the headline is below the fold, so the first success (changing the day and seeing the answer change) happens off screen, and the torn calendar, the page's best picture, needs a scroll. It passes the SPEC numbers (card above 844) but only just.
defects.evidence: Playwright, 390x844 and 390x700, light, fresh load: #result top 680, #result-headline top 790 (below 700 at the shorter height), #grid below 1000. Editing #f-day at y=430 leaves only the badge and buttons visible at 700px.
defects.suggestedFix: Trim the phone stack by 100 to 150px: reduce .sed-intro line-height and font-size under 480px, drop the 'Jump to the explanation' row to share a line with the day label, tighten .hdc-card padding and gaps, or move the 'Try a famous date' select into the More panel on phones. Target headline top at or under 650px at 390 wide.

defects.title: More panel reopens after visitor closes it
defects.detail: renderForm calls setMore(true) on every render while vm.openMore is true (Read my date as is not auto, or a second date is set). A visitor who closes More with such a setting active sees it pop open again at the next edit, pushing the result down about 300px on a phone.
defects.evidence: 390x844 touch: open More, set Read my date as to Julian, tap Fewer options (panel hides), type 14 in Day: after 500 ms #more-panel is visible again.
defects.suggestedFix: Remember the last openMore value in view.js and call setMore(true) only when openMore goes from false to true (or on the first render), so a manual close sticks until the setting is cleared and set again.

defects.title: Copy link in error state copies stale link
defects.detail: With an invalid field (current.state is null) the Copy link button skips the hash rewrite and copies location.href, which still holds the last valid date, then says 'Link copied.' The link does not match what is on screen.
defects.evidence: 1280x800: open #p=england&d=11&m=2&y=1731, clear Day, More options, Copy link to this date: status 'Link copied.', clipboard http://127.0.0.1:PORT/#p=england&d=11&m=2&y=1731 while the card shows the day error.
defects.suggestedFix: In the btn-link branch, when current.state is null call view.flashCopied(false, 'link') or disable btn-link while the result tone is error.

defects.title: Invalid field not marked for assistive tech
defects.detail: The error message appears in the result card and is announced through the live region, but the offending field gets no aria-invalid or visual mark, and the error card keeps a 28rem min-height that leaves a large blank card on desktop.
defects.evidence: 1280x800: clear Day: #f-day has no aria-invalid, no highlight; card shows the red message and about 250px of empty paper (screenshot critic-tmp/d-error.png).
defects.suggestedFix: In render(), set aria-invalid=true on the control named by fields.error.field (day, month, year, place, custom group) and remove it otherwise; artisan can add a red border for [aria-invalid=true] and drop min-height for [data-tone=error].

defects.title: Header links under 44px tap height
defects.detail: The 'Jump to the explanation' link is 36px tall and the back pill 40px; every other control meets 44px.
defects.suggestedFix: Give .sed-jump and .sed-back min-height 44px (padding-block on the jump link).

defects.title: No-JavaScript note sits after the explainer
defects.detail: With JavaScript off the result card reads 'Loading the converter...' and the only explanation is the noscript paragraph at the very end of the page.
defects.evidence: Playwright context with javaScriptEnabled false at 390x700: #result-headline text 'Loading the converter...'; noscript text exists only after the footer.
defects.suggestedFix: Move the noscript paragraph to just under the intro so it shows beside the dead card.
